snippet: Hey Jordan, Attaching the first full round of creative for Gather, the holiday campaign. This is the concept we walked through at kickoff, now fleshed out across hero, email, and p
body_text:
Hey Jordan,

Attaching the first full round of creative for Gather, the holiday campaign. This is the concept we walked through at kickoff, now fleshed out across hero, email, and paid social formats.

Quick rundown of what's in the deck:

1. Hero concept - warm, low-lit tablescape photography, three color stories (Cranberry, Sage, Oat) that map to our three gifting collections. This replaces the bright studio-white look we used for spring/summer.
2. Typography - we're proposing a new display serif (Canela) for headlines only, keeping body copy in the existing Inter family so it doesn't feel like a full rebrand, just a seasonal shift.
3. Email templates - three variants ready: gift guide, countdown/urgency, and the post-Cyber-Monday "still shopping" nudge. Ben's lifecycle team already has the countdown one in Klaviyo as a draft.
4. Paid social - 9x16 and 1x1 crops for both the hero tablescape shot and three product-only cutdowns, plus a UGC-style set shot on a phone for TikTok that intentionally looks less polished.
5. OOH concept (stretch, budget-dependent) - a single static board concept for the Domain and South Congress locations if Wes can find room after the agency renewal numbers settle.

Things I need from you specifically before this goes to Sofia for final sign-off:
- Confirm the Cranberry palette doesn't clash with the new sitewide banner color once the replatform ships (I don't have visibility into what Anchor & Vine locked in).
- A gut check on whether the Canela headline treatment reads too editorial for our customer - it's a departure and I want your read before I fall in love with it.
- Sign-off on using the phone-shot UGC set for TikTok even though it wasn't part of the Northlight shoot brief; we'd need Hollis to add a half day for it.

I know Q4 is a lot right now with the agency contract and the site migration both live. Happy to walk through this live tomorrow if that's faster than comments in the deck. Target is to lock hero direction by the 18th so production has runway.

One more thing while I have you: I want to loop the popup and cart-abandonment flows into this too, since right now they're still running the spring photography and it'll look jarring once the homepage flips over to Gather. Ben's team can swap the creative in Klaviyo quickly once we have final assets, but I'd rather we plan for it now than scramble in October. Same question applies to the order-confirmation email template, which nobody ever thinks about updating seasonally but customers do see it right after checkout.

On budget and timeline: production cost for this round, assuming the TikTok add, comes in around $6,800 for stock, styling props, and Northlight's day rate beyond what's already covered in the retainer. Wes has a placeholder for it in the Q4 creative line but I wanted you to have the real number before it surprises him. Full asset delivery timeline, if we lock direction by the 18th, is first selects by August 20th and a complete set - email, paid social, and site imagery - by September 5th, which still gives the replatform team time to drop the new imagery into staging before their freeze.

Rachel

Rachel

subject: Re: FTC disclosure language for Linen Cut partnership
snippet: Jordan, Here's where things stand post the FTC's updated endorsement guidance. Three things to build into the contract and the creative brief: 1. Disclosure placement - #ad or #spo
body_text:
Jordan,

Here's where things stand post the FTC's updated endorsement guidance. Three things to build into the contract and the creative brief:

1. Disclosure placement - #ad or #sponsored has to be unavoidable, meaning it can't be buried in a string of hashtags at the bottom of a caption. For Reels specifically, the FTC wants it in the video itself (on-screen text or verbal) as well as the caption, not caption-only anymore. Give Amara's team the exact language: "Paid partnership with Habitat Goods" using Instagram's built-in Paid Partnership tag, plus a spoken or on-screen "#ad" in the first three seconds.

2. Giveaway mechanics - if the mechanic is "tag a friend to enter," we need official rules posted somewhere (a linked page is fine), no purchase necessary language, odds of winning, entry period start/end dates, and eligibility (18+, US residents, employees of Habitat Goods and immediate family excluded). I'd also recommend capping it at one entry per person to avoid it reading as a sweepstakes requiring a bond in Texas - if you want, I can draft the official rules page copy, just tell me the entry window.

3. Material connection disclosure survives even if we don't pay her directly in cash - since she's getting product plus a fee, that's a material connection regardless of amount, so the disclosure requirement applies in full either way.

Send me the final contract once it's drafted and I'll do a quick pass before it goes to her for signature. Should be a fast turnaround on my end.

snippet: Sofia, Wanted to get ahead of this before it lands on your desk as a surprise line item in the FY27 budget review. Fold & Field sent over their renewal terms for the SOW that expir
body_text:
Sofia,

Wanted to get ahead of this before it lands on your desk as a surprise line item in the FY27 budget review. Fold & Field sent over their renewal terms for the SOW that expires September 1, and I want to walk you through where I've landed and why, since it's a meaningful increase.

THE ASK: They're proposing the monthly retainer move from $22,000 to $25,500, with the increase justified by formalizing TikTok content production as a scoped deliverable rather than the ad hoc billing we've been doing all year. Separately from that, they haven't taken a rate increase in the two years we've worked with them, which given agency comp inflation is honestly reasonable on its face.

WHAT I'VE VALIDATED: I pulled our actual TikTok spend with them for the trailing 12 months - we paid roughly $2,800/month in ad hoc production fees on top of the base retainer, so the "new" $3,500/month increase is only about $700/month more than what we're already spending unofficially. Framed that way, this isn't really a $42K/year new cost, it's closer to $8,400/year in true incremental spend, with the benefit of predictable invoicing and a formal SLA around TikTok turnaround times, which has been a pain point - Cam's flagged more than once that ad hoc TikTok requests get deprioritized against retainer-covered work.

WHERE I HAVE CONCERNS: Their creative production line (shoot days, editing) hasn't changed in scope but the base retainer for that work is going up too as part of the "modest rate adjustment," and I don't have great visibility into whether that portion is fair market or just came along for the ride with the TikTok ask. I've asked Tessa for a scope-by-scope breakdown rather than one bundled number so we can evaluate each piece on its own, and I'll push on that Thursday.

MY RECOMMENDATION: I think we renew, with TikTok formalized, but I want to negotiate the base retainer increase down or get something added in exchange - options include an extra shoot day per quarter, or holding the base rate flat and only paying for TikTok as new incremental scope. I also want a 60-day-or-less termination clause preserved given how much of our Q4 execution now runs through them.

I don't need a decision from you today, but I do want your gut check before I go into Thursday's call, and I'll loop Wes in parallel on whether $25,500-30,000/mo range is even fundable given everything else in the FY27 marketing budget. Let me know if you want 15 minutes before Thursday or if written is fine.

Jordan

snippet: Hi Jordan, Monthly status update for the replatform migration ahead of our sync on Monday. Here's where things stand as of this morning. COMPLETED SINCE LAST UPDATE: - Product cata
body_text:
Hi Jordan,

Monthly status update for the replatform migration ahead of our sync on Monday. Here's where things stand as of this morning.

COMPLETED SINCE LAST UPDATE:
- Product catalog import: all 1,140 SKUs migrated from the legacy Magento instance into Shopify Plus, including variant options and metafields for the collection taxonomy your team built.
- Redirect map: 480 legacy URLs mapped to their Shopify equivalents to protect SEO equity, submitted to Denise's team for a spot check.
- Theme build: PDP, PLP, and homepage templates are functional on staging, built against the current brand system.

IN PROGRESS:
- Inventory sync between the new platform and your 3PL (Deliverr) is the long pole right now. We found a mismatch in how bundle SKUs report available quantity that's taking longer to resolve than scoped - roughly a week behind where I hoped we'd be.
- Klaviyo integration for email/SMS is connected and passing test events, but historical customer profile data (purchase history specifically) is still backfilling, expected done by end of month.
- Payment processing: Shopify Payments is live in test mode, Braintree fallback still needs configuration for the small percentage of international orders you flagged as a requirement.

RISKS TO FLAG:
- The inventory sync delay puts real pressure on our target cutover date. If it slips another two weeks we're cutting it close to your holiday campaign launch, and I don't want to be the reason Gather launches on a broken cart experience.
- We have not yet load-tested checkout under Black-Friday-level concurrent traffic. I'd like to schedule that for the first week of September at the latest, which means we need a stable checkout build about two weeks before that.

PROPOSED REVISED TIMELINE:
- Aug 1: inventory sync resolved, bundle SKU issue closed
- Aug 15: full site freeze for QA on staging
- Sept 1: load test
- Sept 15: cutover, roughly two weeks later than the original plan

I know that's not the news you wanted given Gather launches in early November, but it still gives comfortable runway before peak. Let's align on Monday and I can walk through the bundle SKU issue in more detail if useful.

A couple of other items for the sync: QA coverage right now spans Chrome, Safari, and Edge on desktop plus Safari and Chrome on mobile, which covers about 94% of your current traffic mix per the analytics export you sent in April. I don't think we need broader coverage than that, but flag if your assumptions have changed. On SEO, beyond the redirect map, we've also rebuilt the structured data (product schema, breadcrumbs) since the legacy site's markup was out of date and was probably costing you some rich-result real estate in search already.

Last thing - once inventory sync is resolved, I'd like to run a full content audit against the legacy site to make sure nothing customer-facing got dropped in the migration, things like the sizing guide PDFs and the FAQ accordion content tend to get missed. I can have someone on my team start that in parallel with the sync fix so it doesn't add time to the critical path.

Kyle

subject: Modern Retail mention this morning
snippet: Jordan, Flagging something before you see it elsewhere - Modern Retail published a piece this morning in their "Sourcing" newsletter titled "The gap between what DTC home brands sa
body_text:
Jordan,

Flagging something before you see it elsewhere - Modern Retail published a piece this morning in their "Sourcing" newsletter titled "The gap between what DTC home brands say and what they ship," and Habitat Goods is named, not as the main subject but in a section about sustainability claims. The specific line: a former employee (unnamed, described only as "a former merchandising staffer") is quoted saying the "responsibly sourced" language on our linen and wood product pages overstates what's actually verified, and that internally the standard was "vendor self-attestation, not third-party certification."

CONTEXT: This isn't a fabrication, exactly - our sourcing claims page does rely on supplier questionnaires rather than something like GOTS or FSC certification for most SKUs, which has always been true and is disclosed (thinly) in a footnote. The unflattering framing is new, the underlying fact pattern mostly isn't.

SCALE: This is not a viral moment. The newsletter has a trade audience of maybe 40,000 subscribers, mostly retail/DTC operators and journalists, not consumers. I've seen it shared by two industry accounts on LinkedIn so far with neutral, not-outraged captions. No consumer press has picked it up as of 9am.

RECOMMENDATION: I don't think this warrants a public statement or correction - that would draw more attention than the mention currently has. What I do think we need:
1. A short internal talking point for Sofia and the exec team in case anyone gets asked about it directly (by press, by a retail partner, at a conference).
2. A look at whether we want to quietly firm up the sourcing claims language on the site - not as a reaction to this piece, but because the underlying gap is real and someone else could raise it again with more reach.
3. I'd hold off reaching out to the reporter. Engaging tends to extend the life of a story that would otherwise die in 48 hours.

Want to sync at 2pm today? I can have the talking points draft ready by then.

For what it's worth, this is a fairly normal pattern for a company our size once you're doing enough volume to attract trade press attention - I've handled three or four of these for other DTC clients this year alone, usually tied to sourcing, labor, or return-policy claims, and the ones that turn into real problems are almost always the ones where the brand goes on the defensive publicly rather than just quietly tightening the underlying practice. I don't think this is that, but wanted to give you the pattern-matching context rather than just the recommendation.

Priyanka
